title: Forward sweep read update
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet and let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$ with $k$ work tapes. Choose $a_0\in\Gamma$, a configuration $c$ of $M$ on a word $y\in\Gamma^*$, a state $q$, integers $a,z$, a natural number $n$, an input-head position, an output word, and left and right stacks. Starting from the forward-sweep configuration whose read table is initialized from $c$ at coordinate $a$ and whose right stack contains the ordinary encoding of the blocks at coordinates $a$ through $a+n-1$, after $nk$ steps the simulator is in the forward-sweep configuration whose read table is initialized from $c$ at coordinate $a+n$ and whose frontier is $z+nk$. Its left stack is the reversed encoding of those blocks with preceding-block head flags recorded, followed by the original left stack; its right stack and output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
